A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Dual Attention Transformer research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Relational Games, mathematical problem-solving, Tiny Stories, and ImageNet experiments, including appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 reports original Relational Games, mathematical problem-solving, CIFAR, and FineWeb-Edu experiments, alongside retained Tiny Stories results and additional analyses.

M1.justification: The relational-attention operation, three symbol assignment mechanisms, and dual-attention blocks remain. v2 incorporates Grouped Query Attention into its vision and language DAT variants (Appendices C.3–C.4), introducing parameter sharing beyond v1's documented ordinary multi-head configurations.

E1.justification: v2 adds FineWeb-Edu language modeling and CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 image recognition, while removing ImageNet evaluation. Relational Games and the five mathematical tasks remain. Tiny Stories remains in Appendix D.3, although its broader main-text evaluation disappears.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated PrediNet, CoRelNet, and Abstractor comparisons on Relational Games (Figure 7), substantially expanding comparison with specialist relational architectures. These are distinct from the DAT-with-RCA substitution comparisons retained from v1 in Appendix D.

E3.justification: Relational Games gains Transformer head-count and width controls; mathematical evaluation expands from two-layer models to two–four-layer comparisons with additional wider Transformers. New CIFAR protocols use 4-by-4 patches, 100 epochs, and alternative augmentation procedures. FineWeb-Edu introduces approximately 350M–1.3B models, GPT-2 tokenization, 1,024-token contexts, and a 10-billion-token budget. These are expanded or new settings, rather than matched reruns of v1's experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds CIFAR symmetry and augmentation studies (Tables 3–4) and a learned-relation interpretability case study (Figure 5). It removes the mathematical extrapolation analysis and Tiny Stories symbol-assignment and symmetry ablations. Relational Games symmetry and both RA-versus-RCA analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Five-seed bootstrap 95% confidence intervals remain for Relational Games and mathematics. v2 adds mean-plus-standard-error reporting in the mathematical results table and reports ten-seed CIFAR experiments; v1's ImageNet results lacked comparable uncertainty reporting. This extends reporting practices without establishing an increase in runs for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Substantial result blocks are added or replaced. v2 Table 1 reports CIFAR-10 accuracy of 89.7% for ViDAT versus 86.4% for ViT; Table 5 reports FineWeb-Edu perplexity of 16.09 for 343M DAT versus 16.94 for the 353M Transformer. Mathematical model-size results and specialist-baseline findings are also added, while ImageNet and broad Tiny Stories results disappear. These new-setting comparisons do not establish v1-to-v2 performance gains.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and Appendix A's assumptions and proof remain substantively unchanged. Appendix B.1 adds a memory-complexity argument: aggregating relations before projection avoids an O(b n² dmodel) intermediate, using O(b n² dr) relation storage instead, with a stated connection to standard-attention memory scaling.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain relational attention and its integration with sensory attention for efficient learning across modalities. v2 adds an explicit parameter-efficiency claim to the abstract and contribution list, extending v1's emphasis on data efficiency without redefining the central architectural contribution.

C2.justification: v2 interprets learned relation activations as semantic structure, adds a scaling-law interpretation, and discusses trade-offs against specialist architectures with stronger inductive biases. It removes much of v1's Tiny Stories ablation-based discussion of symbol choice and syntax. The configuration and hardware-optimization limitations remain, with mechanistic interpretability added as a substantive research direction.

D1.justification: v2 expands parameter and tensor descriptions, documents a memory-saving contraction order, and supplies technical recipes for the new experiments. It reports a new implementation repository, a Python package, and publicly available pretrained weights. Conversely, detailed Tiny Stories settings disappear despite retained Appendix D results, and the mapping between mathematical decoder configurations and reported results remains unclear.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning through cognitive and inductive-bias literature, neural scaling laws, visual reasoning, and mechanistic interpretability. Appendix C.1 adds substantive discussion of DAT's generality versus specialist relational architectures. The existing RA–RCA distinction remains; citation renumbering itself is only stylistic.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, and the method exposition systematically introduces 'sensory attention' terminology. Repeated symbol-motivation text is removed, Appendix B is reorganized and expanded, and the vision and language subsections exchange order. These changes substantially reshape the narrative beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: v2 replaces mathematical epoch curves with parameter-size plots and introduces language-scaling plots, token-relation visualizations, dataset examples, and mathematical/CIFAR tables. Relational Games plots gain comparator curves and parameter-count legends. The symmetry and RA-versus-RCA plots are reused and relocated, rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support by addressing v1's explicitly untested language-model scaling and adding parameter-count controls and specialist relational baselines. Replicated CIFAR results and expanded implementation/access information further improve assessability. These gains outweigh the loss of ImageNet, mathematical extrapolation, and several Tiny Stories ablations, although DAT-only Grouped Query Attention and unclear mathematical configuration reporting still limit attribution.
